critique: The nearly black indigo ground, five-color cell palette, cool violet controls, and restrained typography form a cohesive scientific-visualization system. The sphere is impressive but its construction reveals roughness: the grid extends and clips irregularly near the limb, the right edge collapses into a hard dark wedge, cells at the boundary are abruptly cut, and the thin orbital ring intersects the silhouette without a consistently resolved front/back treatment. Cell sizes and glow vary somewhat arbitrarily, weakening the sense of one simulation grammar. The panel is orderly, but native range tracks and thumbs look browser-default beside the custom buttons and swatches, and internal section spacing leaves an unusually large dead middle region.
suggestion: Mask and warp the grid and cells cleanly to the sphere, add a controlled atmospheric rim, and explicitly split orbital lines into behind/in-front segments so every intersection is intentional. Define discrete cell-size, opacity, and glow states tied to the five palette roles instead of random variation. Restyle sliders, thumbs, swatches, dividers, and buttons from one component token set, then redistribute panel sections on a consistent vertical rhythm so the controls occupy the available surface without a vacant gap. Normalize tiny uppercase label contrast and align all values to one right edge.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
